neighbours.label: Names of molecular-biology assay techniques, peaking on their acronym or compound pieces (micro|bead, (F|ISH), (FF|PE), (EL|ISA)); describing the same measurement in plain words does not fire
fire: Antibody levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
Copy number was confirmed by quantitative PCR (qPCR) in all samples.
Protein binding sites were mapped by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP).
Archived biopsies were analysed as formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) sections.
Plasma markers were measured with a bead-based multiplex immunoassay panel.
Tumour sections were stained by immunohistochemistry (IHC) for the receptor.
Rearrangements were detected with fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) probes.
Transcript levels were profiled using RNA microarrays in the genomics core.
quiet: Antibody levels were written down by the nurse at every visit.
Copy number was confirmed by the lab manager in all samples.
Protein binding sites were discussed by the authors in the paper.
Archived biopsies were stored in the basement for many years.
Plasma markers were measured at the local clinic every month.
Tumour sections were examined by the senior doctor for the report.
Rearrangements were described in detail in the second chapter.
Transcript levels were reported in a table at the end of the study.

predictions: Assay names in methods prose reach 0.4-0.85 on a piece of the name; the same sentences with plain verbs ('measured by the nurses', 'described') stay under 0.1.
